title: Regularity of the polynomial parameter map over a prime field
statement: Let k be a field isomorphic to Q or F_p, p prime, and B a commutative regular local k-algebra. Let d be a natural number equal to the Krull dimension of B and t:Fin d→B generate the maximal ideal. Then evaluation k[X_i]→B sending X_i to t_i is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Completeness of B is not assumed. This includes d=0.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 07DY; More on Algebra, Tags 07PS, 07PV, 0H7U, 07C0; original node steps 2–4.

proof.text: Localize the polynomial ring at the origin ideal. The origin is maximal with residue field k, and its localization is regular local of dimension d with the coordinate variables as generators. The parameter evaluation contracts the maximal ideal of B to the origin, so it extends to a local map A→B.
A minimal generating list of the regular local target B is regular. Apply the regular-parameter flatness criterion to A→B, with the polynomial coordinates in A. Its closed fibre is B/n over k.

The prime field k is complete at its zero maximal ideal and is therefore a G-ring. Its polynomial ring is a finite-type G-ring, so the completion map of A is regular. Finite purely inseparable extensions of k are trivial: characteristic zero fields are perfect, and Frobenius is bijective on F_p. Thus every finite purely inseparable base change of the field B/n is isomorphic to B/n and is regular Noetherian.

The local closed-fibre regularity criterion now makes A→B regular. The target B has one maximal ideal and localization there is B itself. Its contraction is the origin. Apply the maximal-local criterion to conclude that the polynomial parameter map is regular. The zero-dimensional case has empty parameters and field target.
